readout_other: Motor-evoked potentials (MEP), short-interval intracortical inhibition (SICI) and facilitation (SICF) via paired-pulse TMS; motor section of the Unified Parkinson's Disease Rating Scale (mUPDRS)
direction_notes: tbTUS increased MEP amplitude at 30 min post-stimulation (LTP-like plasticity) in healthy controls and PD patients on dopaminergic medication, but not in PD patients off medication; the mUPDRS bradykinesia subscore was reduced at 60 min in PD-on but not PD-off.
safety_notes: The participants did not report any adverse effect.

target.label: primary motor cortex (M1), FDI hot spot

device.model: custom 2-element annular array transducer (500 kHz, 38 mm diameter, 10 mm thickness)

timing.protocol_description: One pulse train of 80 seconds delivered to M1 (theta-burst pattern, tbTUS), pulse duration 20 ms, repetition interval 200 ms (PRF 5 Hz), fundamental frequency 500 kHz, duty cycle 10%, power setting 20 W/cm2; sonication depth set to 30 mm to approximate scalp-to-cortex distance; white noise masking delivered through earphones during the 80-s sonication.

source_quotes.n_subjects: We studied 20 (5 women, age: 59.1 8.7 years [mean standard deviation]) mild to moderate PD patients diagnosed by a movement disorder specialist based on the MDS criteria<sup>22</sup> and 17 age-matched healthy controls (5 women, age: 63.7  9.5 years).
source_quotes.randomised: PD patients were studied in both the on (taking usual PD medications) and the practically defined off (overnight withdrawal of medication—minimum 12 hours) states on two different days at least 72 hours apart in random order.
source_quotes.auditory_control: We delivered white noise to subjects through earphones during sonication (80 seconds) at an intensity of 50% to 70% of the maximum volume (based on each subject’s tolerability) to mask the auditory effects of tbTUS.
source_quotes.adverse_events: The participants did not report any adverse effect.

flags.reason: Paper reports two distinct groups (20 PD patients, 17 healthy controls) rather than a single sweep; recorded as a list.

The 20 W/cm2 'power setting' used to measure ISPPA/ISPTA in free water is not unambiguously stated as the measured free-field ISPPA value itself; interpreted as such because the derated in-situ values are given immediately afterward.

No sham condition was used; only the video rater for mUPDRS was blinded. Classified as 'single' blinding (rater) but this does not reflect blinding of the TUS intervention itself, which was open (all groups received active tbTUS).
PD patients attended two sessions (on/off medication); number of sessions for healthy controls is not explicitly stated.

provenance.notes: Case-control study (PD-on, PD-off, healthy controls); no sham TUS condition. Free-field vs in-situ (skull-derated, 75% attenuation assumption) intensities both reported for the same exposure.
